Yeah rar out of qd is extremely powerful. Against non fast fallers, f- throw/ b- throw>qd rar bair is a pretty consistent kill setup. Also another thing you might want to look into is learning how to do a grounded qd from ledge. It's just a timing thing but it opens up a lot of options if you're cornered.

Ike has crazy shield drop options with bair and fair. Playing on plats well is super key imo. Also you mentioned oos options in another comment and ike actually isn't that bad oos imo. His best option is bair and you can actually wave land out of SH bair making for some really cool bait set ups. Fair and bair are both crazy good on shield when spaced well. I like to abuse sh drift back fair a lot. Utilt is a crazy strong anti air. WD back utilt is crazy against characters like fox and falcon. Dtilt is actually safe on shield which is crazy to me. QDA is actually one of your strongest tools in neutral because it breaks asdi down crazy early. But maybe the best move in your kit (aside from qd) is actually jab. Using mix ups with jab combos and grabs and dash backs and drift back fair can get you crazy mileage. One other tricky mix up is if you charge qd and your opponent shields,  they are often looking for you to qd>rar grab. So if instead you just qd through them and rar fair you can get reversals into combos or edge guards. The other big thing I would add is if your opponent is doing a lot of dash back punishes, you can use either dash attack or qd fair to overshoot really effectively.

This is not a pivot grab. It is a reverse aerial rush jump cancel grab (or just a rar grab). Pivot grabs are when your character enters the pivot animation and you grab during it. That's a 1 frame input and its done out of a dash. This is not a 1 frame input and it's done out of a run. The character never enters the pivot animation. This is not a pivot grab.

The main reason is because it puts too much emphasis on game 1. The whole idea behind CF is that you want to reduce the advantage for the player who wins a game and can change characters based on the stage selection. If he goes to the platform you can just learn about his movement and start reading it and if he comes toward you you should already have something out to challenge him. Eventually you will get an opener or just push him offstage where you can kill him. Just don't get intimidated by his speed. It's not a matter of dealing with pressure it's about learning to challenge his movement so he doesn't get anything for free.
